sep6.caption:
Looking for a practical way to support someone in your community? By registering an RACG project, your Rotary Club can help deliver financial assistance to individuals and families experiencing hardship.

The RACG program began through the generosity of Dick and Pip Smith, whose initial donation was then matched by Rotary Clubs across Australia. Together, these contributions have helped countless Aussies in immeasurable ways.

Dick and Pip have since added to their contribution, inspired by the impact that collective community giving can achieve. Register an RACG project now with your local Rotary Club to receive matched funding of up to $15,000.

Register your project today: https://rawcs.org.au/register-a-new-project/

𝗡𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗹 𝗵𝗮𝘀𝗻'𝘁 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗱 𝗮𝘀𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴. 𝗡𝗲𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗵𝗮𝘀 𝗥𝗼𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘆.
Weeks on from the flooding disaster, whole communities are still without safe shelter, still short on food, still rebuilding from nothing. The emergency didn't end when the headlines moved on, and the need hasn't either.

RAWCS and our Rotary partners are continuing relief efforts on the ground, delivering shelter, food and essential supplies to the families still recovering. This is what standing with Nepal looks like for the long haul, not just the first response, but the follow-through.

RAWCS is mostly known for the overseas projects Rotary Clubs run, but there's a fair bit happening underneath that too. RARE ships donated medical and educational equipment. Medishare handles surplus medical consumables specifically. ARAM works on malaria elimination closer to home, in our own region. And a small communications team keeps the training, reporting and public materials running for everyone else.

It's a lot more moving parts than most people realise.

Learn more: rawcs.org.au

sep5.caption:
Many of the children in this project's care walked for days into Thailand, alone or with their siblings, to escape the war in Myanmar. Without Thai identification, they can't go to school, see a doctor properly, or travel freely, so getting that ID sorted is often the first real step toward a normal life.

Borderless Friendship, run through the Rotary Club of Melville, helps with that, along with hostel accommodation and schooling. $3,000 covers a weekend workshop for 50 teenagers on health and relationships education, one of the more practical parts of what they do.

There's a short video on the project page if you'd like to see the community it supports.

More on this project, and how to support it, here: https://directory.rawcs.com.au/26-2014-15

𝗡𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝘀 𝘄𝗮𝗹𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝗿𝘂𝗯𝗯𝗹𝗲.

A rolled up mattress. A quilt. A red bucket, a bag with whatever could be saved. This street was someone's home. Now it's collapsed walls and debris, and the people who lived here are carrying out what's left of their lives, a volunteer in a vest walking beside them.

Nepal has asked for help. Rotary Australia World Community Service (RAWCS) is one of the ways Australia can answer, working through trusted partners on the ground so your donation reaches families directly, not just quickly announced.

If you're in a position to help today, even a small amount matters. Clean water. A tarpaulin. A first aid kit. Or simply cash, so a family can decide for themselves what they need most.
Thank you for standing with them.

https://directory.rawcs.com.au/ProjectDisplay.aspx?17-2026-27

Donations are tax deductible in Australia.

Keeping all seven running costs about $14,887 a year, food, bedding and the basics, and most of that still needs to be raised. Every donation is tax deductible.

sep12.caption:
A Compassionate Grant won't fund just anything, and there's a reason for that. The money needs to go to a person or a small group genuinely struggling, not a general community fund, and it has to be for something specific rather than a broad ask.

If your Club's had an idea but wasn't sure it fit, it's worth a quick check against the criteria rather than guessing either way.

rawcs.org.au

sep15.caption:
Only about 1 in 100 rural girls in the part of Tanzania where Orkeeswa Secondary School operates make it as far as Year 11 or 12, in a region where most families live on less than $1.25 a day. Students at Orkeeswa are beating those odds, topping national exams, and a good number return afterwards to teach in their own community.

The newest classroom needs an outdoor learning space, some AV equipment and two whiteboards. $12.50 covers a whiteboard, $50 covers a piece of AV equipment, and $125 covers a section of the outdoor space.

There's a short video of the school and its students on the project page if you'd like to see it.

You can support this project here: https://directory.rawcs.com.au/ProjectDisplayBB.aspx?5-2011-12
Watch the video here: https://player.vimeo.com/video/256892640

adhoc-mtwoko2z.caption:
Nepal and Australia are 8,000 kilometres apart, but the Rotary community closed that distance in a day. 

When the Trishuli corridor was buried on 26 August 2026, taking hundreds of lives and leaving more than 10,000 households without shelter, Nepali Rotarians turned to their neighbours and Australian Rotarians turned to their phones. Same handshake, same promise, two hemispheres. 

In this radio snippet, Prue Bentley of Radio Australia speaks with Rajendra Gautam, Past President of the Rotary Club of Kathmandu, and Rotary District 9780 Governor Tonie Thiel.
They cover what Rotarians on the ground are seeing and how clubs in Nepal and Australia are working together. 

Rotary District 3292 is mobilising volunteers for relief distribution, while RAWCS has opened the Nepal Flooding Disaster Relief Fund, channelling donations through Rotary contacts in Nepal for shelter, cash grants and clean water.

Every club can play a part. 
Put it to your board this week.

Give what you can today and help a family through the night. 
https://directory.rawcs.com.au/17-2026-27

Donations of $2 or more are tax deductible in Australia.

adhoc-mtwosatu.caption:
#RotariansInAction
More than two weeks after Nepal's Trishuli corridor was buried, the need has not eased. It has simply moved out of the headlines.

Over 10,000 households remain without shelter following the flooding on 26 August 2026. Rotarians in Nepal are still working through the same channels that make disaster response effective: local contacts, quick decisions and funds that reach families directly, without delay or red tape.

If you hold a position on a board or committee, you already know how far a modest allocation can go when a club chooses to act. This is one of those moments where a decision made this week changes what a family has tonight.

RAWCS's Nepal Flooding Disaster Relief Fund puts your donation straight into the hands of Rotary contacts on the ground, for shelter, cash grants and clean water.

Put it to your club this week. A steady contribution now still buys a family a dry night and a hot meal.
https://directory.rawcs.com.au/17-2026-27

Donations of $2 or more are tax deductible in Australia.

sep2.caption:
For more than twenty years, the Tender Foot Self Help School has been part of daily life in Nairobi's Kangemi slum, offering food, clothing and a nursery-to-Grade-8 education to children who would otherwise go without. It has run continuously since 2003.

That kind of consistency depends on the Rotary Club of Emerald & District, and on the people who give to this project year after year.

You can support this project here: https://directory.rawcs.com.au/ProjectDisplayBB.aspx?1-2003-04

sep3.caption:
The Lighthart Project looks after forty children and young people with cognitive or multiple disabilities in Stung Mean Chey, on the outskirts of Phnom Penh, many of whom would otherwise be left out of school altogether.

Some sensory equipment donated from Australia has recently reached the classroom. Beyond that, what the project needs is fairly ordinary: books, desks, teacher salaries, and rent to keep the classroom itself open.

You can find out more and support this project here: https://directory.rawcs.com.au/ProjectDisplayBB.aspx?140-2010-11

sep4.caption:
In Goma, in the Democratic Republic of Congo, a group of mothers called Mama Wimbi sew backpacks, uniforms and school supplies for children who have fled violence and arrived with nothing.

A SchoolKit means one less thing for a family to worry about when they're already stretched between food, housing and school fees. A spare uniform matters too, since clean water is scarce and one uniform can't always be washed often enough to avoid scabies outbreaks in crowded classrooms.

Because the kits are made locally rather than shipped in, a donation also supports the women doing the sewing, and helps them provide for their own children.

There's a short video on the project page showing how the kits are made. You can read more and support the project here: https://directory.rawcs.com.au/ProjectDisplayBB.aspx?23-2023-24

extra.caption:
Millions of people in Ukraine continue to face the devastating impacts of the ongoing crisis, with urgent needs including food, medical aid, safe shelter, mental health support and essential supplies.

Through the Ukraine Crisis Appeal, more than 1.2 million people have received food and clothing, 77,000+ people have received mental health care and $29 million in medical aid** has been delivered, including 11 ambulances. More than 140,000 safe shelter placements and 742,000+ hygiene and first-aid kits have also been provided.

Every number represents a person, a family or a community given hope.

Donating through RAWCS supports the Ukraine Crisis Appeal and its work alongside Caritas Ukraine, UNBROKEN, Tabletochki and other humanitarian partners. The appeal is volunteer-led, meaning almost every dollar donated goes directly towards supporting people affected by the crisis. All donations over $2 are tax deductible.

extra.caption:
What you're watching is the devastating reality of the flooding in Nepal.

Rooftops disappearing under mud, a bridge folding into the river, neighbours pulling each other back before the water reached them. By the time it settled on 26 August 2026, hundreds of lives were gone and thousands of families had nowhere left to sleep.

Rotarians didn't wait to be asked twice. They're already on the ground and RAWCS is now the bridge for Australians who want to help.

Every dollar through the Nepal Flooding Disaster Relief Fund goes to shelter, cash grants and clean water, delivered through people who know these villages by name.

Nepal needs our help. If you're able to give, even a small amount gets there directly, and it gets there fast.

Donate here: https://directory.rawcs.com.au/ProjectDisplayBB.aspx?17-2026-27

extra.caption:
When flooding takes a family's home, it takes more than shelter. It takes clean water, warm bedding and the small comforts that make a day feel livable.

That is what moved the Rotary Club of Dhading to act. With funding support from RAWCS, the club stepped forward for households in Bidur Municipality, Nuwakot, who had lost or left behind their essential belongings when the Bhotekoshi flood forced them into temporary community centres.

The relief initiative asked one simple question: What do these families need most right now? It answered with the essentials: bedding, cooking utensils and a way to start again.

That is Rotary's service ethos in action, showing up with the basics before anyone has to ask twice.

The need has not stopped since. Whatever you can give goes directly into the same support, reaching a family who is rebuilding from almost nothing.

Rotarians and Rotary Clubs are invited to an exclusive live information session on the RAWCS and Airbnb.org Emergency Accommodation Program.

When: Tuesday 6 October 2026, 2:00pm AEDT (Sydney time)
Presenters: RAWCS CEO, Mahir Momand and Airbnb.org representative, Hannah Bellamy
Open to: Rotarians and Rotary clubs ONLY

When a bushfire, flood or major disaster occurs, people often lose their homes or are unable to return for periods at a time. Our Rotarians have stepped in time and time again and assisted their communities going through such difficult circumstances.

The RAWCS partnership with Airbnb.org, will enable responders and eligible individuals and families affected by bushfires, floods and other crises to receive up to 28 nights of free temporary accommodation.

Rotary Clubs and Districts will step in to identify those in their communities that need this support and facilitate this process.

Join us during this webinar to learn how the program runs, who is eligible, and how Rotary Clubs and Districts can use it when disaster strikes.

Any Rotarian or Rotary club who is interested should send an email to info@rawcs.org.au to get the webinar login details.

Please share this with fellow Rotarians in your club.
